items.title: Wycliffe Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: Wycliffe has performed with an impressive array of jazz artists to date, including Al Grey...

ctx.x: Well let me put it this way. Some people have said that the young musicians get their own bands a lot sooner than some of the fellas like Sweets Edison and Al Grey and all those guys. Does that seem to be true in your case?

In our generation I think that does happen. In my case I think that I waited a little while, I played with Wynton for almost, since ’89, eleven, going on twelve years and I’ve had an association with him, I still do. But in terms of acting as a leader there was a time someone had come to me, heard me on a couple of gigs with Wynton and said, “You know you should record a record.” And at that time I felt that I was still in a period or in a stage in my growth where I just wasn’t ready to do that. It was like a…
Yeah. This is where I belong.
